scenes.title: Restart hub
scenes.caption: When the internet stops, try this first.
scenes.say: When the internet stops working, restarting your broadband hub often fixes it. Here's how, step by step.

scenes.title: One device?
scenes.caption: Check if it is just one device.
scenes.say: First, check it's not just one device. If your phone works on Wi-Fi but your laptop doesn't, restart the laptop instead.

scenes.title: Read the light
scenes.caption: Blue is working. Orange has lost connection.
scenes.say: Now look at the light on the hub. Blue means it's working. Orange, or flashing orange, means it has lost its connection.

scenes.title: Off and wait
scenes.caption: Switch off. Wait a full 30 seconds.
scenes.say: Turn the hub off at the power button or the wall socket. Then wait a full thirty seconds, so it clears its memory.

scenes.title: Back on
scenes.caption: Turn it on. Do not switch it off again.
scenes.say: Turn it back on. The light flashes for two to three minutes while it reconnects. Don't turn it off again.

scenes.title: Still stuck?
scenes.caption: Check the cable. Orange over 10 minutes? Ring.
scenes.say: Steady blue? Try the internet. Still nothing? Push the cable in firmly at both ends. Orange for ten minutes means a possible area fault.

scenes.title: Don't reset
scenes.caption: Skip the pinhole reset button unless asked.
scenes.say: One last thing. Don't press the tiny pinhole reset button unless they ask. It wipes your Wi-Fi name and password. To check for a fault, use the service status page or ring the number on your letter.
